question: Controlled: what does the pepM pre-screen cost and change on a dilute full taxon, one taxon, one code version?
method: 2,863 Erwiniaceae genomes, run end-to-end twice on the same commit, identical except pepm_prescreen. GTDB-Tk off in both arms. Params passed in JSON files (run_erwin_screen_{off,on}.json, committed here), never on the CLI: `--pepm_prescreen false` arrives as the string "false", which is truthy in Groovy. bigscape_min_bgc_length=2000 from nextflow.config, confirmed applied in both databases.
why_this_run_exists: It supersedes the uncontrolled Erwiniaceae pair that stood behind the '6.5x' claim. That pair's screen-off arm gave antiSMASH ONE TASK PER GENOME while its screen-on arm batched 50 genomes per task, so close to half the apparent saving was antiSMASH start-up paid 2,771 times over rather than screening. Here both arms batch identically: 57x50+13 genomes off, 6x50+8 on.
controls_verified: antiSMASH task granularity identical (50 genomes per task, both arms)
FETCH_RENAME_SCREEN: 115 tasks in both arms, same genomes fetched
pepm_prescreen is the only differing parameter

the_screens_own_cost.how_measured: FETCH_RENAME_SCREEN is 83.1 CPU-min with the screen on against 14.3 with it off. The screen is no longer a separately timed stage -- a rejected genome is deleted before its output is declared, so it never reaches publishDir -- so its cost is the arm-to-arm delta of the fused process. Both arms run 115 such tasks over the same genomes, so the delta is the screening work and nothing else.
the_screens_own_cost.supersedes: 91.3 CPU-min, which was a PEPM_PRESCREEN stage total from the older uncontrolled pair

recover_orfs_also_shrinks: 257.4 -> 14.0 CPU-min (18x). RECOVER_ORFS only sees genomes that passed the screen, so this is a real downstream saving -- but it is NOT the screen acting on antiSMASH, which is why the headline ratio is quoted on antiSMASH CPU alone.
caveats: antiSMASH CPU-minutes are the comparable column. Whole-pipeline totals fold in RECOVER_ORFS, whose asymmetry is intrinsic to screening rather than a separate effect.
2,863 genomes, not the 2,771 of the 2026-09 runs: the NCBI download grew. Counts are therefore not directly comparable to the older Erwiniaceae records.

The traces here were written by a -resume, which rewrites pipeline_trace.tsv in place. Nearly every row is CACHED and carries the realtime of the session that actually ran it, so any re-analysis must sum CACHED as well as COMPLETED.
